problem: The heading and the first sentence say 'six components', but the text then names seven: generator, condenser, expansion valve, evaporator, absorber, pump and solution heat exchanger. The figure shows only six (no solution heat exchanger), so a student cannot tell whether the count is wrong or the heat exchanger is not being counted.
fix: Say 'seven components (six if the solution heat exchanger is left out)' or write 'The main loop has six components; a solution heat exchanger is usually added' so the count matches the list and the figure.

problem: The trapped expression TE/(TG − TE) is the Carnot COP of a work-driven refrigerator running between TE and TG. It is not the reversible limit of an absorption cycle, which involves three temperatures, TE, TG and the condenser/absorber temperature TC. A student may read the trap as saying that TE/(TG − TE) is the correct reversible absorption COP, only misapplied.
fix: State the reversible absorption limit properly, TE(TG − TC)/[TG(TC − TE)], and warn that no formula based on three or two temperatures is used for rating; the rating is the measured ratio QE/(QG + Wp).
